review.finding: DTD guard is a raw byte-substring check; a BOM-carrying UTF-16/32 report spells '<!DOCTYPE' with NUL bytes, evades the check, and expat would still parse its internal DTD. Low impact (runner's own pytest writes UTF-8; modern expat caps amplification; no external entities) but the docstring says refused outright.
review.suggestion: Decode strictly as UTF-8 first (add UnicodeDecodeError to except), run the DOCTYPE check on the text, ET.fromstring(text). Add a UTF-16 DOCTYPE test.

summary: One low finding; callers safe (all fall back to whole-unit retry); urllib3 bumps complete.
